title: Jonah Flees and the LORD Sends a Storm
summary_text: The LORD's word sends Jonah to speak against Nineveh's wickedness, but Jonah boards a ship for Tarshish instead. When the LORD sends a violent storm, the sailors cast lots and discover that Jonah is responsible. Jonah tells them to throw him overboard, and after failing to row ashore, they do so while asking the LORD to spare them. The sea becomes calm, and the sailors fear the LORD, offer a sacrifice, and make vows. The LORD appoints a great fish to swallow Jonah for three days and nights.

title: Jonah Thanks the LORD for Rescue
summary_text: Inside the fish, Jonah prays about calling to the LORD from the depths of Sheol, the realm of the dead. He recalls sinking beneath the waves and says God raised him from the pit as his life faded. His prayer reached God's holy temple. Jonah says those who cling to idols abandon God's loving devotion, and he promises thankful sacrifice and fulfilled vows because salvation comes from the LORD. At God's command, the fish vomits Jonah onto land.

title: Nineveh Turns from Evil and Is Spared
summary_text: When the LORD's word comes again, Jonah goes to Nineveh and warns that the city will be overturned in forty days. The people believe God and respond with fasting and sackcloth. Their king joins them and orders people and animals to fast, while everyone must call to God and leave evil and violence behind. He hopes God may turn from His anger and spare them. Seeing their changed actions, God relents from the threatened disaster.
key_points: Jonah obeys the LORD's renewed word and announces Nineveh's overthrow in forty days.

title: The LORD Questions Jonah's Anger
summary_text: Angry that God has withheld disaster, Jonah says he fled because he knew the LORD's compassion and loving devotion. He asks to die, then waits outside the city to see what happens. The LORD contrasts Jonah's concern for a short-lived plant with His own concern for Nineveh's many people and cattle.
